verified_title: Cosmos Policy: Fine-Tuning Video Models for Visuomotor Control and Planning
problem: A pretrained video generator does not directly accept robot proprioception or produce executable action chunks and calibrated outcomes. Demonstration-only world/value models see predominantly successful behavior and can rank out-of-distribution action proposals incorrectly.
contribution: Cosmos-Predict2-2B is fine-tuned through latent-frame injection without adding modality heads: the same diffusion backbone learns a policy, observation dynamics and empirical-return prediction. A second checkpoint trained on actual rollout outcomes supports best-of-N planning while the original checkpoint proposes actions.
algorithm: Insert normalized repeated proprioception, flattened action chunks and scalar returns into VAE latent frames, alongside current/future multiview images. Conditioning masks select policy, world-model or value tasks, with initial batch allocation 50/25/25. Rollout refinement changes this to 10/45/45. Direct control jointly samples outputs and discards future/value outputs; planning autoregressively samples actions, future observations, then values and ranks proposals.
observations: Language/T5-XXL embeddings, current measured joint/EE proprioception and camera images. Only current and chunk-end observations are used, not image history or a complete future video. ALOHA uses 14 joint angles, overhead plus two wrist cameras. The paper explicitly treats partially observed images/proprioception as approximate state.
actions: Embodiment-specific normalized chunks: LIBERO16 steps all executed; RoboCasa32 predicted/16 executed; ALOHA50 joint commands at25Hz, all executed before querying. ALOHA controller frequency is deliberately reduced from50Hz; these are experimental choices, not Explorer controller settings.
embodiment_and_data: LIBERO four suites,10 tasks each,50 demonstrations/task; RoboCasa24 tasks with50 human demonstrations/task; ALOHA two ViperX300S arms and185 demonstrations across language object placement80, shirt folding15, candy collection45 and ziploc45. Policy training filters failed demos while dynamics/value training includes them. Planner refinement uses648 real rollouts, including505 from evaluations of all five compared policies plus143 additional Cosmos ziploc rollouts.
experiments: LIBERO500 trials/suite×3 seeds=6000; RoboCasa50 trials/task×24×3=3600. Every direct ALOHA method gets101 fixed initializations:30 placement,20 folding,25 candies,26 ziploc, with explicit ID/OOD splits and partial-completion rubrics. ALOHA comparisons match48h on8H100 for large models; DiffusionPolicy uses1H100. Planner tests two harder tasks after training on recorded successes and failures.
baselines: DiffusionPolicy, Dita, pi0/pi0.5, OpenVLA-OFT(+), CogVLA, UniVLA, UVA, UWM, VideoPolicy, GR00T variants and FLARE. Simulation tables include published methods with unequal demonstration counts; physical methods receive the same185 demos and fixed initial states. Ablations remove auxiliaries, initialization and joint objectives; planner compares predicted-future V(s') with Q(s,a).

limitations: Physical scores permit partial credit and do not establish complete sock-task success. Aggregate ALOHA improvement coexists with worse OOD average than pi0.5. Full2s open-loop chunks and H100 inference pauses limit dynamic interaction. Planner needs costly on-distribution successes/failures, and its648-example pool includes prior evaluation rollouts rather than being an untouched test set. Planning is shallow best-of-N; observation/value prediction is not identified contact physics or guaranteed calibration.
code_and_license: Paper p11 states release of code, checkpoints and data through its project website. Source implementation, checkpoint terms, dependencies and dataset licenses were NOT_AUDITED here; no software was executed. A release statement is not license clearance.
hardware_adaptation: COMPARE offline against the already implemented compact ACT/PPO pilot. Explore a small future-observation auxiliary head and outcome-trained value ranking only after collecting source-bound actual episodes; do not claim the2B model or8-H100 planner runs at the paper's latency on a16GB Jetson. Pi overview-only camera differs from ALOHA's three views, and Explorer/SO101 action dimensions, coordinate scales and calibration differ from14D ViperX commands.
algorithm_detail: For a K×d action chunk, normalize each dimension to[-1,1], flatten, repeat into a latent volume and average repeats on extraction; scalar values are similarly repeated. Four identical copies/image align with the Wan VAE's temporal compression, after a blank initial frame. Training corruption uses70% original log-normal noise and30% uniform[1,85]; inference sigma_min4/sigma_max80 rather than original near-zero minimum. Return labels are Monte-Carlo discounted terminal outcomes. Planning keeps the original policy and a rollout-refined world/value checkpoint, samplesN8 actions,3 future observations/action and5 values/future, then majority-mean aggregates bimodal predictions.
integration_contract: Offline input must contain timestamped actual camera frames, measured/declared-basis proprioception, an explicit joint/action schema, chunk timing, and episode outcomes. Fit normalization only on training episodes; preserve camera/frame IDs, source hashes and train/eval splits. Adapter outputs a typed predicted chunk and separately tagged synthetic observation/value; it cannot relabel generated images as camera evidence. An experiment must document whether inference overlaps execution, rather than silently changing existing Explorer controller timing.
license_evidence: NOT_AUDITED. Primary paper release statement p11 does not establish the license of Cosmos base weights, derived policies, tokenizer or training corpora.
required_experiments: Compare compact ACT with identical demonstration budget and camera views against ACT plus future-observation supervision, using held-out episode/object splits and independent full-task successes.
Train value/dynamics on genuine success and failure episodes separate from final evaluation; test calibration and ranking under dropped views, occlusion and shifted object positions.
Measure end-to-end inference, memory and completed-chunk timing on the actual NX before considering a direct-control role; H100 latency cannot be reused.
Report complete task success separately from per-stage score, especially bag opening, cloth grasp stability and repeated recovery.
difference_from_explorer: Paper hardware is a calibrated14D bimanual platform with wrist views and large H100 training budgets. Explorer has different kinematics/camera coverage and currently demonstrated engineering pilots rather than an equivalent185-demo cloth dataset or validated long-horizon sock manipulation. The transferable idea is joint supervision plus outcome-based evaluation, not a ready hardware policy.
